title: Two incidents at once
story: A traffic spike on one stack and an OOM on another, simultaneously. Expected: both healed in parallel.

args.summary: Raised worker-b memory limit from 128m to 384m to accommodate observed batch sizes (180 MiB payloads causing rss 132-143 MiB) that exceeded the old 128m limit and triggered repeated OOM kills.

timeline.note: watching for 3× the crash interval (10–60) s with no crash or OOM

timeline.thought:
ROOT CAUSE: worker-b was repeatedly OOM-killed (exit 137, oom_killed=true, 3+ restarts in ~1s) because job batch size jumped from 60 MiB to 180 MiB, pushing process RSS to 132–143 MiB against the container's 128 MiB memory limit ("rss 138 MiB > limit 128 MiB", "rss 143 MiB > limit 128 MiB").

CHANGE: Raised the memory limit for worker-b from 128m to 384m via set_resources, giving headroom above the observed ~180 MiB batch footprint (plus worker overhead), then applied via apply_fix.

GUARDRAILS: Within policy — single stateful=false worker capped at 1 replica (min=max=1, unchanged), memory 384m is well under max_memory 512m and max_total_memory 1g, and set_memory is the only/allowed action used; no image/env changes made.

FOLLOW-UP: Monitor mem_peak_mb over the next few batches since batch size "grows with customer data" per the service notes — if peaks approach 384m again, consider raising further (up to 512m max) or adding batch-size capping/partitioning logic in the app itself.

args.summary: Scale web-b from 1 to 2 replicas to relieve CPU saturation (peak 51.9% vs 50% per-replica limit) causing intermittent request-queueing timeouts; stateless service, scaling is the allowed action.

timeline.note: waiting for the median of 5 probes < 500 ms (≤ 60 s; an improvement is never rolled back)

timeline.thought:
ROOT CAUSE: CPU saturation on the single web-b replica — cpu_pct_peak_total hit 51.9% against the 50%-per-replica limit (0.5 cpus), causing request queueing/timeouts (probe spikes to 1800ms, 983ms, 1780ms vs 800ms threshold, 3 breaches) and the client-side BrokenPipeError in logs (client timing out while waiting). Average CPU (11.1%) is low, consistent with bursty traffic exceeding the single replica's throughput ceiling (~20ms CPU/request × limited cpus).

CHANGE: Scaled web-b from 1 to 2 replicas (no memory/cpu change) — service is stateless, behind traefik with label-based discovery, and "scale" is the only allowed guardrail action for this service.

GUARDRAILS: Within limits — replicas 2 ≤ max_replicas 3 (min 1), memory and cpus per replica unchanged (128m/0.5 cpu, under max_memory 256m), total memory well under max_total_memory 768m. Dry-run validated with no violations before apply.

FOLLOW-UP: Monitor latency/CPU for the next few cycles; if peak CPU per replica still approaches 50% under load, escalate to raise max_replicas or cpus limit in watchdock.md, or investigate whether traffic bursts warrant further scaling to 3 replicas.
